chapters.summary: Dominique Jones, Executive Director of Global Kids, says CBOs serving 30 schools can reinforce Portrait learning through global citizenship programming and evaluation expertise. She suggests joint hearings with the youth committee and DYCD to leverage resources.
chapters.title: Dominique Jones says community-based organizations are key Portrait partners

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Same as the last panel, we'll start on my right, your left, and go down.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Dinowitz, for the opportunity to speak and to really talk about this important topic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: I'm going to turn in my written testimony, but just to kind of focus on a few points.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: One of the things that I think we are kind of missing in this conversation around Portrait of a Graduate is the ecosystem around schools that can actually help to support them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: I represent Global Kids.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: I'm the executive director, and we serve 30 schools, one as a community school provider as well as after-school provider.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: We are going to be central in this conversation about the implementation of Portrait.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: We actually are organizations that can actually enhance and also deliver on certain programming, such as our global citizenship programming, which, you know, Global Kids has been working through for 38 years and providing those leadership services

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: to our schools.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: And so I think it's important that we start to have the, you know, it's great that we're talking about the pedagogy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: approach, the instruction, you know, shifting assessment to portfolio assessment, but there has to be supporting organizations that are supporting services that can help to reinforce, enhance that learning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: And I think that organizations like mine and other CBOs will be instrumental to that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: I think also we also provide some expertise resources that can help around evaluation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: And I know that's something that you talked about all day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: I've had the opportunity to listen to you speak to those things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: We have some of the infrastructure to support that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: We also are thinking about how do we measure the impact of interventions on the whole child.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: And so I think that that's important.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: We should talk about it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: One thing I think is also we need to be having joint hearings with the youth committee, bringing DYCD and DOE together so that they can begin to think about how we can partner and leverage those resources.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique Jones
utterances.text: You know, we as a community school provider are there every day working with kids, families, and we really want to be able to make sure that portrait is a success.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Teresa Ranieri, a veteran NYC educator, says Portrait begins with youngest learners and requires recurring funding for teacher professional learning, coaching, intervention, and family engagement. She warns donations alone will not sustain it.
chapters.title: Teresa Ranieri asks for baseline funding for NYC Reads and Solves to support Portrait

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: My name is Teresa Ranieri, and I've been an educator in New York City public school system for over 30 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: The portrait of a graduate begins with our youngest learners in kindergarten, as they learn to think critically, communicate effectively, and use what they've learned beyond the classroom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking for the council for baseline funding for New York City and New York City Solves so that we can help create this portrait of a graduate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: We need to provide recurring funding so my children are prepared to be these young adults we heard today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: It goes beyond a curriculum.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: It is teacher professional learning, time for collaboration, coaching, and implementation support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: Not only has it been successful in my school, students decode and write, but it goes beyond that with vocabulary and background knowledge.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: Aligned with your portraits of a graduate, we complete inquiry and research projects, go on field trips supporting modules,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: and these are the foundations for capable readers, effective communication, critical thinkers, engaged citizens that we want all of our students to become.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: I've heard you say repeatedly today, and I was very happy, what support are our teachers going to have?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: Teachers need continued professional learning and coaching so they can make thoughtful instructional decisions and respond to the students sitting in front of them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: Students who need additional support need access to targeted intervention and tutoring.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: Family needs me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: meaningful opportunities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: We need to invest in the educators that are before all of our students, kindergarten through high school.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: But my concern is this won't happen with donations if there's not baseline funding so that our kindergartners can be those that you saw today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And just one point to make about that.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I appreciate the recognition that

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: You hear this committee talk a lot about training teachers, and you hear from the Affinity Network say it isn't just a couple of trainings.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: It is deep, engaging work that needs to be done.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: One of the elements of the $280,000 we got for the Youth Journalism Coalition, like so much other funding, it helps leverage private funding.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: But you have, you know, this council is committed to investing in the things that we know work and help educate our students.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And so, you know, I won't talk more about the money, but again, I'll reiterate, this can be done internally through the DOE, through our professionals here, not through

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: outsized contracts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: Wood outside contractors are those, and they are mostly not-for-profit organizations, but they come in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: eight, ten times a year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: They're not a part of the community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Teresa Ranieri
utterances.text: They don't know our children, the families, the teachers, and that speaks volumes.

chapters.summary: Joni Rivera, Assistant VP at New York Foundling, says Portrait must include stability, belonging, self-advocacy, and supported transition for foster youth. She cites Road to Success's 88% graduation rate and asks for early identification, coordination, and investment in individualized models.
chapters.title: Joni Rivera says foster care students need stability and support to reach Portrait

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Okay, and our final in-person panelist.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Zanowitz and members of the Committee on Education.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: My name is Joni Rivera, and I'm the Assistant Vice President of Educational Services at the New York Foundling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: Thank you for this opportunity to testify on the New York's Portrait of a Graduate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: For students who have experienced foster care, the Portrait of a Graduate must reflect more than academic achievement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: It must also include stability, belonging, self-advocacy, healing, and a supported transition into adulthood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: The New York Foundling has served children, families, and communities for more than 150 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: Through our education and child welfare work, we see every day that nearly 500 young people in foster care we serve are capable, resilient, and full of potential.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: But too often, their path to graduation is complicated by placement changes, school transfers, transportation barriers, trauma, missed services, and uncertainty about what comes next.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: Programs like the Foundlings Road to Success show what is possible when students receive consistent, trauma-informed academic support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: Road to Success pairs nearly 2,000 students with tutors who also serve as mentors, coaches, and advocates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: While the overall graduation rate

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: For New York City students in foster care is 42%.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: Students participating in Roads to Success achieved an 88% graduation rate last school year of 2026.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: Students like Lisa and Jared remind us why sustained support matters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: Lisa graduated while navigating disrupted placements and uncertainty about her college transition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: Jared, an English language learner, was one regent's exam away from

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: From graduation and with tutoring and encouragement, improved his score by 26 points and earned his diploma.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: Their stories show that graduation is possible, but support cannot stop at the finish line.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: We recommend that the city strengthen early identification of students who are undercredited, chronically absent, missing services, or struggling with region's requirements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: We also urge stronger coordination among schools, administration for children's services, foster care agencies, caregivers, Fair Futures coaches, tutors, and education specialists.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: Finally, we ask...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: Sorry, finally, we asked the city to invest in proven individualized models like Road to Success so more young people can graduate prepared for college and career.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joni Rivera
utterances.text: Thank you for your time and commitment.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz thanks in-person testifiers and says children are more than test scores. He says the hearing will now move to remote testimony and calls Kaliris Salas-Ramirez.
chapters.title: Dinowitz thanks panels and transitions to remote testimony

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And also thank all of you for your work that you do, you know, recognizing, I think, what so many of us do, but a very rigid system does it, which is that our child and our children are more than just test scores.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: There's so much more to our children.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I would love to see the portrait recognize the incredible work that our kids do and the incredible people that they are.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: So I once again want to thank you for your work and your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: includes the in-person portion of our public testimony.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: We will now move to remote testimony.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: If you are testifying remotely, please listen for your name to be called.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Once your name is called, a member of our staff will unmute you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: You may then start your testimony once the sergeant at arms sets the clock and cues you to begin.

chapters.summary: Salas-Ramirez, CEC4 president and parent of a consortium student with an IEP, says performance-based and inquiry learning helped her son find his voice. She supports Portrait but calls NYC Reads and Solves culturally destructive and not aligned with culturally responsive curriculum.
chapters.title: Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez supports performance assessment but criticizes NYC Reads and Solves

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Khalid Salas, it is you may begin once you are unmuted and the sergeant cues you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: Hi, good evening, Chair Denowitz, and thank you for holding this really important hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: We are in a time of transition in our New York City public schools.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: I do want to disclose, so my name is Kalidi Salas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: I'm the parent of two public school students, and I'm also the president of CEC4.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: And I should also state that my children both attended Central Park East 1 Elementary School, which is the oldest public progressive school in New York City, founded by Deborah Meyer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: In addition, I am a parent of a high schooler in a consortium school.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: So you can imagine that I deeply believe in the use of performance-based assessments, problem-based learning, inquiry-based learning, and an emergent curriculum to support all of our learners, particularly our most vulnerable learners.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: I do want to share that my oldest child has an IEP.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: He suffers from anxiety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: And it has been this type of curriculum that has allowed him to find his voice and has allowed him to develop the skills that he's going to need as he looks forward to being a politician, not a choice of mine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: And so it is really important to create these spaces for young people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: I will also say that I'm a medical educator and 60% of my curriculum is problem-based learning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: So when we're talking about career and college readiness, the portrait of a graduate really resembles what our expectations are in higher education and setting up students for success in terms of

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: of providing them with a deep learning experience rather than just going over content, which, as you mentioned, is one of the methods in terms of teaching to the test or teaching to a regents exam.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: I will also very quickly state that New York City Reads and New York City Solves, these curricula are culturally destructive, and at the center of the portrait of the New York State graduate is culturally responsive curriculum.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: And so I really want to interrogate the notion that New York City Reads and New York City Solves is preparing our children to move forward with these requirements for the portrait of the New York State graduate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: And hopefully we'll be thinking about how we can develop curriculum that is responsive and relevant to our New York City public schools.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Time expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz thanks DOE and all who testified, says much work remains on communication, best practices, and rigor. He asks if anyone else wishes to testify, sees no one, confirms no one on Zoom, and adjourns the hearing.
chapters.title: Dinowitz closes hearing after no additional testifiers

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Although, you know, we have your lot to say what you want to have to forcefully push back and say your child should aspire to be a politician.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: It is a very, it's a great, you know what?

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Because we're here today talking about a critical issue, the critical issue of portrait of a graduate.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And that could be your child on this great dais with these cups, these dentist cups.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: But I do want to thank the Department of Education, all of the people who testified today.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: It's clear that this is an issue that people care about deeply because they care deeply about the future of our city and care deeply about our children.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: It's also clear that there's a lot of work to do, that there are a lot of people outside of the D.A.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: and within the DOE who are being very thoughtful about this work.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: But there is so much more to do in terms of the communication, in terms of sharing best practices, ensuring we are holding ourselves to a very high,

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: rigorous standard so that we are seeing our children for who they are and giving them the best education possible.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: So I want to thank the DOE and everyone who testified.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Once again, and this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Will be adjourned once I read this very important message.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: If there's anyone else present in the room who has not had the opportunity to testify but wishes to do so, please raise your hand.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Seeing no one else who actually wishes to testify.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Anyone on Zoom?

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: There's no one on Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Okay, now I can officially close out the hearing.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you.

summary: The Committee on Education held an oversight hearing on the New York State Portrait of a Graduate and New York Inspires, focusing on how NYC Public Schools will implement new graduation requirements and decouple Regents exams from diplomas.

First Deputy Chancellor Danielle Giunta and her team described existing work on the Portrait, personal finance rollout, work-based learning, and equity plans, while Council members pressed for clearer guidance, standardized rubrics, and better communication with principals, teachers, and families.

Public testimony featured students, educators, advocates, and affinity partners who overwhelmingly supported performance-based assessment and journalism education, but many urged the city to leverage existing consortium and affinity expertise, delay unfunded mandates, and ensure rigor and equity across all schools.
